sections.h2: Green hydrogen at the SIGHT bid is $4.16/kg, against $1.50/kg for grey

chart.title: The competitive green bid sits well above the grey benchmark
chart.source: Post, Sections 3 and 5 (SIGHT Mode-2B bid; global SMR benchmark).

sections.means: Green hydrogen is priced at roughly three times grey, so the switch carries a real cost premium.
sections.todo: Refiners should keep tendering for green hydrogen at these bid prices while tracking how the premium falls.

sections.h2: Per barrel, hydrogen costs $0.76 in grey and $2.12 in green

chart.title: A barrel of diesel needs about 0.51 kg of hydrogen, so green costs $2.12
chart.sub: Hydrogen cost per barrel of BS-VI diesel, US$.
chart.source: Post, Sections 2 and 5; 0.51 kg/bbl is the post's consumption figure.

sections.means: Hydrotreating hydrogen is a small share of a barrel's cost, but the green premium roughly triples it.
sections.todo: Refiners should publish per-barrel hydrogen costs so consumers can see the effect of the switch on diesel.

sections.h2: Full green substitution would add ₹0.55–0.80 per litre, close to BS-VI's ₹1

chart.title: A full switch to green would add about the same as the BS-VI price rise
chart.source: Post, Sections 2 and 5 (this piece's own worked estimate).
rows: Premium, grey to green, full substitution

sections.means: The premium is an illustrative ceiling, not a price move: only 30 KTPA is contracted against about 2.5 MTPA of grey demand.
sections.todo: Government and refiners should track how much of the 2.5 MTPA grey demand is actually switched to green hydrogen.
